note: AI-generated. Referee requests are inferred from the changes between arXiv v1 and the accepted version, not read from reports. The blind review of the new version was not run, so 'blind' is empty.

concerns.asked: Likely: the data do not prove a new form of altermagnetism; define the terms and soften the headline claim.
concerns.response: Title now says 'Signatures of', the abstract 'reveal symmetry signatures' and 'support', and the results 'supporting' (new pp. 1, 4). The introduction defines altermagnetism by the crystallographic relation between opposite-spin sublattices and bi-altermagnetism as both sublattices satisfying it (new p. 1).
concerns.judgment: The likely request was met: the claim is softened throughout and the term is defined.
concerns.still_open: A stricter reader could still ask for a spin-group analysis per sublattice and an observable that separates a bi-altermagnet from an altermagnet with a polarised second site.

concerns.asked: Likely: CD appearing below T_N shows magnetic order, not specifically bi-altermagnetism; rule out other orders such as the nearby ferrimagnetic phase.
concerns.response: New caveat that the CD onset alone does not identify bi-altermagnetism and that the m versus m' selection rule does (new p. 4). A new ferrimagnetic simulation shows CD in both geometries and stronger, unlike the bi-altermagnetic case (new pp. 4-5; Fig. S9, SI pp. 15-16, 22).
concerns.judgment: The argument is now explicit and backed by simulation, but it rests on the single m-plane null measured once and on no characterization of the measured crystal's magnetization.
concerns.still_open: No M(T) or M(H) of the measured crystal and no quantified m-plane residual CD.

changes.summary: Caveat on what CD onset proves

concerns.asked: Likely: give the scattering angles, beam size, polarization degree, helicity flux balance and the normalization of RCP and LCP spectra.
concerns.response: Angles theta and omega are given with every Q (new pp. 2, 3, 5, 6; SI pp. 13, 17, 18). A new SI setup section gives polarization above 98%, beam size and LCP/RCP flux ratio 1.1, and a normalization section explains flux and 5-7 eV normalization (SI pp. 11-12).
concerns.judgment: The requested details are now in the paper.
concerns.still_open: A stricter reader could still want difference spectra with error bars and a quantified CD.

concerns.asked: Likely: could the low-energy CD come from magnons, phonons or vibronic modes rather than local Oh spin-orbital excitations?
concerns.response: New text weighs magnons (10-15 meV), phonons and vibronic modes and argues collective excitations are unlikely to explain the CD because dispersion is small (new p. 5); the SI notes magnons lie under the elastic line (SI p. 12).
concerns.judgment: The question is answered by argument, not new data; the incident-energy dependence of the CD that would pin the site was not measured.
concerns.still_open: No incident-energy CD map and no explicit Td-site CD below 0.15 eV.

concerns.asked: Likely: the two-peak fit next to the elastic line and the 2:3 ratio claim are not robust or are inconsistent.
concerns.response: The 2:3 statement is now conditional and refers to energy spacing, without 'zero-order' (new p. 5). A new SI section describes the constraints and calls the fit 'a constrained minimal decomposition' (SI p. 12).
concerns.judgment: The overstatement was hedged and the method disclosed; whether this satisfies the referee cannot be judged without the report.
concerns.still_open: No fit uncertainties, and the 52 versus 65 meV spin-orbit values and 'minimal momentum dependence' remain.

concerns.asked: Likely: explain more clearly why time-reversal symmetry does not force RIXS-CD to vanish.
concerns.response: The paragraph was rewritten around the experiment's boundary conditions: the time-reversed process does not contribute to the measured intensity, so only unitary symmetries constrain the CD (new p. 3).
concerns.judgment: The explanation is clearer and self-contained.

concerns.asked: Likely: cite prior RIXS-CD work on ferro/ferrimagnets and other altermagnets, and drop the claim that XMCD lacks sublattice resolution.
concerns.response: The comparison paragraph now cites RIXS-CD in CrI3 and a topological ferromagnet, adds alpha-Fe2O3, notes the magnon-CD controversy, and no longer says XMCD lacks sublattice resolution (new p. 4).
concerns.judgment: The positioning is fairer and the overstatement was removed.

concerns.asked: Likely: note that momentum-dependent spin splitting, the hallmark of altermagnetism, is not probed.
concerns.response: A new paragraph says the local-model analysis does not reveal the spin splitting and that ARPES will be needed (new p. 4).
concerns.judgment: The limitation is now stated plainly.

concerns.asked: Likely: explain how the up and down sites of each sublattice enter the model.
concerns.response: The text now says the two Oh (and Td) sites have different crystal-field Hamiltonians related by crystallographic symmetry (new p. 4); the SI adds that sublattices partly cancel in the m' geometry (SI p. 16).
concerns.judgment: The change goes the asked way, but the orientation of local axes and scattering geometry in the simulation are still not given, so sufficiency cannot be judged.
concerns.still_open: No overlay of measured and convolved simulated CD, although agreement is now called quantitative.

concerns.asked: Possibly: show sample quality and orientation.
concerns.response: New Fig. S1 shows the mounted sample and a Laue pattern; crystal growth moved to the SI (SI p. 11).
concerns.judgment: Characterization is now shown, but the number of samples and cooldowns is still not reported.
concerns.still_open: Reproducibility on a second crystal or mount is not shown.

concerns.response: Source data for the figures are deposited on Zenodo (new pp. 7, 9); code is available on request.
concerns.judgment: The data request is met; this may have been journal policy.
